  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Erev Shabbat Parshat Va'etchanan,</t>
    <t s="2">the fifteenth of Av, 5738*</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section notes that the text is an unedited draft.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">(A draft.</t>
    <t s="1">Not proofread.)</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the order of Torah and mitzvos in the two paragraphs of Shema, and the precise language used for Torah study in each.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And you shall teach them to your children and speak of them,"</t>
    <t s="1">and afterwards it is stated, "And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="2">the mitzvah of tefillin,</t>
    <t s="3">about which our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="4">"The entire Torah is equated to tefillin,"</t>
    <t s="5">the intention of which is regarding the mitzvos of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="6">and this means,</t>
    <t s="7">that the verse precedes the matter of Torah to the matter of mitzvos.</t>
    <t s="8">And it is known the precise observation of our Nesi'im,</t>
    <t s="9">that in the second paragraph of Shema it is stated,</t>
    <t s="10">"And you shall bind them as a sign upon your hand, etc., and you shall teach them to your children, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="11">that this verse is in reverse order,</t>
    <t s="12">preceding the matter of mitzvos</t>
    <t s="13">(the mitzvah of tefillin)</t>
    <t s="14">to the matter of Torah.</t>
    <t s="15">Also, one must understand what is the reason that the order where Torah precedes mitzvos is specifically in the first paragraph of Shema,</t>
    <t s="16">and the order where mitzvos precede Torah is specifically in the second paragraph of Shema.</t>
    <t s="17">Also, one must understand the precise language regarding the matter of Torah,</t>
    <t s="18">that in the first paragraph it is stated, "And you shall sharpen them, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="19">according to Rashi's explanation</t>
    <t s="20">(from the midrashim of our sages, of blessed memory),</t>
    <t s="21">that it is an expression of sharpening,</t>
    <t s="22">that they should be sharp in your mouth, so that if a person asks you something</t>
    <t s="23">(a halachah)</t>
    <t s="24">you will not need to stammer over it, but rather tell him immediately</t>
    <t s="25">(and only afterwards is it stated, "and speak of them"),</t>
    <t s="26">whereas in the second paragraph it is stated, "And you shall teach them, etc.,"</t>
    <t s="27">which this term includes all modes of study</t>
    <t s="28">(even if the study is not in a manner of being sharp in your mouth, etc.).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
